newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin man spared jail for sex with teen girlfriend.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin man spared jail for sex with teen girlfriend.

text.p: A 19-year-old man was spared a prison sentence Tuesday for having sex with his underage girlfriend after jurors who convicted him of sexual assault asked the judge to be lenient.

Kevin Gillson was sentenced to two years probation, and now he and his 16-year-old girlfriend await the birth of their child expected this week. Gillson could have received 40 years in prison from Ozaukee County Court Judge Thomas Wolfgram.

Gillson had testified that he intended to marry his girlfriend, who was 15 at the time she became pregnant. The couple had told their parents, attended marriage counselling with a pastor and Gillson had quit school and taken a job to support his young family.
"He is a good young man," their counsellor, the Rev. George Jorenby of the United Church of Christ, said.

The judge ordered Gillson to perform 100 hours of community service and to finish high school, required him to undergo counselling including advice on parenting skills, and required him to report to state probation officers as a sexual offender.

Although the girl testified that their sex was consensual, Wisconsin law does not allow anyone under 16 to give consent and Gillson was convicted by a jury of sexual assault on a child. Some jurors cried when delivering their guilty verdict April 17 and asked that he not be given prison time.
Ozaukee County District Attorney Sandy Williams ignored widespread criticism of her decision to prosecute Gillson, and Gov. Tommy Thompson's office said the Republican would consider pardoning him.
